examples.text: „Den Tag verbringen die unscheinbar gefärbten Nachtschwalben unbeweglich am Boden oder auf Ästen, nachts jagen sie Insekten, die mit dem kurzen, aber weit gespaltenen Schnabel gefangen werden.“

glosses: nicht eindeutig, uneinheitlich in Ansichten oder Meinungen

examples.text: Viele Nationen haben heute zunehmend gespaltene Gesellschaften: die Briten und die Schotten wegen des Brexit, die Polen pro oder contra ihrer Regierung, ganz Europa wegen der Flüchtlinge, in den USA die Amen und die Reichen, etc, etc.

Der Titel war noch nicht erfunden. Doch mit den Geschehnissen und erst recht den weitreichenden Folgen des Konstanzer Konzils wäre das Bodenseestädtchen locker Kulturhauptstadt Europas geworden. Drei Päpste, eine gespaltene Christenheit, ein konfliktreiches Europa - da war viel zu regeln und noch mehr zu versöhnen.

Wer kämpft in Syrien gegen wen? - Eine in zahlreiche Rebellengruppen gespaltene Opposition und internationale Mächte, die an verschiedenen Fronten mitmischen - der syrische Bürgerkrieg ist unübersichtlich.

glosses: An opening, fissure, or V-shaped indentation made by or as if by splitting.

examples.text: The river flows through a cleft in the mountains.
Then came some palsied oak, a cleft in him / Like a distorted mouth that splits its rim / Gaping at death, and dies while it recoils.

To syntactically separate a prominent constituent from the rest of the clause that concerns it, such as threat in \"The threat which I saw but which he didn't see, was his downfall.\

examples.text: This may be so because in most languages the most natural clefting involves NP's, and it is in fact hard in most languages to cleft the verb, although some — notably Kwa languages in West-Africa — allow such clefting.

The strategy the language employs is to cleft the clause containing the wh-phrase, as exemplified in (3) […]

translations.source_sense_description: durch Spaltung in zwei oder mehrere Teile geteilt

glosses: Divided into two branches.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: bifid, bipartite, bilobar, bilobular, split, forked

Elizabeth's disturbing presentation of herself as both virginal and sexual bifurcated after her death into opinion about whether she was virginal or sexual, so that on the one hand Elizabeth was apotheosized as the saint who through her refusal to marry had kept England Protestant and free, while on the other hand she was still the object of detraction by persons such as “one Sheapheard, a barrister of Lincolns Inn, [and] a base Jesuited papist,” who during James I's reign uttered ”base and scandalous” words regarding the late queen's honor.

glosses: simple past and past participle of bifurcate

glosses: To divide fully or partly along a more or less straight line.

examples.text: The critical component of the photosynthetic system is the “water-oxidizing complex”, made up of manganese atoms and a calcium atom. This system splits water molecules and delivers some of their electrons to other molecules that help build up carbohydrates.
He has split his lip.
a huge vessel of exceeding hard marble split asunder by congealed water

glosses: To break along the grain fully or partly along a more or less straight line.
To share; to divide.

examples.text: We split the money among three people.
Presently the 57-strong Class 378 fleet is split between the East London line and North London line, with 29 units allocated on the east side.

glosses: To leave.

examples.text: Let's split this scene and see if we can find a real party.

glosses: To separate.

examples.text: Did you hear Dick and Jane split? They'll probably get a divorce.

glosses: To (cause to) break up; to throw into discord.

examples.text: Accusations of bribery split the party just before the election.

glosses: To factor into linear factors.

examples.text: In the first case X²-2, the minimum polynomial of #92;sqrt 2, splits completely over #92;Q(#92;sqrt 2); in the second case we see that X³-2, the minimum polynomial of 3#92;sqrt 2, does not split completely over #92;Q(3#92;sqrt 2).

examples.text: The ship splits on the rock.

glosses: To burst out laughing.

examples.text: "[…]I split, and tell all […]"

examples.text: Boston split with Philadelphia in a doubleheader, winning the first game 3-1 before losing 2-0 in the nightcap.

glosses: To vote for candidates of opposite parties.

examples.text: He’s got a nasty split.

A split shot or split stroke.
A dessert or confection resembling a banana split.
A unit of measure used for champagne or other spirits: 18.75 centiliters or one quarter of a standard 75-centiliter bottle. Commercially comparable to ¹⁄₂₀ (US) gallon, which is ¹⁄₂ of a fifth.
A bottle of wine containing 37.5 centiliters, half the volume of a standard 75-centiliter bottle; a demi.
The elapsed time at specific intermediate points in a race or speedrun.

examples.text: In the 3000 m race, his 800 m split was 1:45.32

glosses: A tear resulting from tensile stresses.
A division of a stake happening when two cards of the kind on which the stake is laid are dealt in the same turn.
A recording containing songs by multiple artists; a split single or split album.
The division of a single taxon into two or more taxa; as opposed to a lump.

examples.text: [I]t would be a rare split in that it would be unlikely to result in an armchair tick for any birders, living or dead.
